Present: Mr. Tarun Deora, Advocate
 for the petitioners.
Mr. Gautam Thapar, Sr. Dag, Punjab.

** **
Aaradhna Sawhney, J. (Oral)
1.

Status Report dated 07.10.2025 by way of affidavit of Mr. Kamaljit Singh, Deputy Superintendent of Police (Headquarters), Tarn Taran, has been filed on behalf of respondents No.1 to 3.-State,
which is taken on record.

In para 4 thereof, it has been pointed out that petitioners have joined the investigation but did not fully cooperate in the same as in they did not get recovered the amount (of respondent No.4) fraudulently, pocketed by them.
Thus, as per the investigating agency the custodial interrogation of petitioners is needed.
Further, in para 6, the role of the petitioners has been highlighted.

2. During the course of submission, it came to the notice of the Court that without exhausting the remedy of filing the anticipatory bail application before the learned Sessions Judge, petitioners have directly approached this Court by way of filing the present petition.
1 of 3

3. A query was also posed to learned counsel for petitioners as to what was the extra ordinary situation/circumstances prompting both the petitioners to directly approach this Court, without exhausting the alternate remedy.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent No.4/complainant is a Police Official,
who has been continuously harassing both the petitioners and threatening to involve them in criminal cases.
Learned counsel has also drawn the attention of the Court to the order dated 02.08.2025 passed by this Court, vide which both the petitioners were granted the concession of interim bail.

For the sake of convenience, the said order is reproduced as under:-
"This is a petition for anticipatory bail under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 in case bearing FIR No.341 dated 10.07.2025 under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B IPC, 1860 registered at Police Station Goindwal Sahib, District Tarn Taran.

The case of the prosecution is that the petitioners have accepted Rs.01,09,30,000/-
for providing various properties to the complainant and the petitioners had received Rs.20.77 lakhs in cash as an earnest money and outstanding 88.52 lakhs were received through various bank accounts but they did not provide any flat to the complainant.
Learned counsel for the petitioners contends that they did not have any direct dealing with the complainant, they had only introduced the complainant-party with the main accused.
However, it is also stated that Rs.87 lakhs have been returned by the petitioners to the complainant through bank account transfer.
He further states that the petitioners are willing and ready to join the investigation.
Notice of motion for 16.09.2025.
Mr. Kamalpreet Bawa, DAG, Punjab, accepts notice on behalf of the respondent-State and seeks time to file reply.
May do so positively before the next date of hearing with a copy in advance to the learned counsel opposite.
2 of 3

sentences.text: 4. Heard.

5. In view of the request of learned counsel, present petition is dismissed as withdrawn with direction that till the filing of the anticipatory bail application before the Court of Sessions, no coercive steps be taken against petitioners.

Mr. Kamalpreet Bawa, DAG, Punjab, accepts notice on behalf of the respondent-State and seeks time to file reply.
2 of 3
In the meantime, the petitioners are directed to appear before the SHO/Investigating Officer as and when called upon to join investigation and in the event of their arrest, they shall be released on interim bail on their furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of SHO/Investigating Agency, subject to the following conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) of the BNSS [erstwhile Section 438(2)
Cr.P.C.]:-
i) that the petitioners shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
ii) that the petitioners shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
Harwinder Singh And Another vs State Of Punjab And Others on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35150137/
2 iii) that the petitioners shall not leave India without the prior permission of the Court;
iv) such other condition as may be imposed under sub-section (3) of Section 480, as if the bail were granted under that section."
However, learned counsel for the petitioners wishes to withdraw the present petition with the prayer that till the filing of the anticipatory bail application before the Court of Sessions at Tarn Taran,
petitioners, who are otherwise on interim anticipatory bail, be protected.
5. In view of the request of learned counsel, present petition is dismissed as withdrawn with direction that till the filing of the anticipatory bail application before the Court of Sessions, no coercive steps be taken against petitioners.
